The word *waqa'a* (وقع) indicates that something has fallen from above in a necessary fall that no one can prevent. We say that gravity (al-jadhibiyyah) is what brought it down. This root appears in matters of great importance that carry awe, as in His saying: ﴿And when the word has come to pass upon them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth that will speak to them...﴾ (82) [An-Naml]. He also said: ﴿So the truth came to pass, and what they had been doing was rendered void﴾ (118) [Al-A'raf], and He said: ﴿He said, "Indeed there has fallen upon you from your Lord abomination and wrath"﴾ (71) [Al-A'raf].

So, *waqa'a* signifies a decisive matter that is accomplished in itself, by the command of God, who determined it and fixed it to occur in this form. It is like an alarm clock that you set to wake you for the dawn prayer. When the alarm rings at dawn and wakes you, the credit and greatness do not belong to the alarm, but to the One who set it for that time. Likewise, when the truth comes to pass, the greatness belongs to the One who brought it about.

Thus the word *waqa'at* (وقعت) means: it is an event that has occurred and cannot be averted. God, glorified is He, said: ﴿When the Inevitable Event occurs﴾ (1) [Al-Waqi'ah]. That is, the Resurrection has already occurred in principle and in its ordering, as though it had actually happened, because the One who speaks these words is God, the Truth, whose command no one can repel.

For this reason He named it *al-waqi'ah* and said after it: ﴿There is no denying its occurrence﴾ (2) [Al-Waqi'ah], because they used to deny it and reject resurrection after death. God, the Truth, informs us about the Resurrection as an event that has already taken place, so that there is no denying its occurrence, as though it had already happened.

God, exalted is He, named it *al-Waqi'ah*, and it has several other names, each with its own meaning. He gives us a glimpse of this terrifying and dreadful day. Reflect: they are *al-Tammah* (the Overwhelming), *al-Haqqah* (the Inevitable), *al-Qari'ah* (the Striking), *al-Sakhkhah* (the Deafening Blast), and *al-Waqi'ah* (the Event). Each one has its own aspect, and together they comprise all these meanings from different angles at the same time.

The final category is "and the foremost, the foremost" (wa-al-sabiqun al-sabiqun). He repeated it for emphasis. These, although they come last in the mention, are first in rank, and they are the highest of the degrees, as evidenced by the fact that He, glorified is He, reported about them saying: ﴿Those are the ones brought near﴾, meaning: brought near to the Throne. So if you want the order from highest, then the foremost, then the companions of the right hand, then the companions of the left hand.

Thus these are three degrees which their people occupy in the Hereafter according to their deeds in this world. The foremost is a person who blessed his life with good deeds from his youth, then remained upon this until he died, so he preceded others to Paradise. The companions of the right (or the right hand) are a person who in the early part of his life, from his youth, was doing evil, but his self-reproaching soul (nafs al-lawwamah) caught him, so he repented, turned back to God, and remained upon doing good until he was taken. The companions of the left (al-mash'amah) are the man who in the early part of his life did evil, and remained upon that until he was taken.

Paradise is the gift of God, and in it the companions of the right and the foremost gather together, except that the foremost are in a higher station and closer to the Throne. Where are ﴿those brought near﴾? In the Gardens of Bliss. We understand this from the words of the Exalted in Surat az-Zumar:

﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups until, when they reach it and its gates are opened, and its keepers say to them, "Peace be upon you; you have done well, so enter it to abide eternally."﴾ (39:73) [az-Zumar]... Then He said after it: ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne...﴾ (39:75) [az-Zumar]

Thus, nearness here means nearness to the Throne.

The foremost here is the one who competes with others to outdo them, and the competition here is in goodness, which is something legally desired (matlub shar'an). Therefore the Truthful, glorified is He, commanded us to hasten and to compete: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth...﴾ (3:133) [Al 'Imran] And He said: ﴿Race to forgiveness from your Lord...﴾ (57:21) [al-Hadid]

The race is a race of faith and righteous deeds: a race in which one wants to outdo, while at the same time loving for his brother what he loves for himself, a race free of spite and selfishness.

The believer competes with others, and the matter is clear in his mind: the rewards await the one who gets ahead, and the gift is a gift that does not run out. What is remarkable is that the believer hastens to do good in his life, and he may even hasten in his death out of longing for the Garden, whose signs he saw while in the throes of death.

And their reward is (﴿rest﴾). They said: it means mercy from Allah and joy in the blessing of Allah. Mercy's breadth and loftiness are proportionate to the one who shows it, so when the mercy comes from Allah, it is mercy without limit.

The companions of the right (Ashab al-Yamin, "the People of the Right") are the second category. He did not elaborate on the bliss they find, but was content to describe them in a way that indicates bliss: "they are in peace" (﴿فَهُمْ فِي سَلَامٍ﴾). Some of them greet others, each group greeting the next. Or the angels greet them, or Allah, glorified and exalted, greets them, as He says in Surah Ya-Sin: "Peace, a word from a Lord who is Merciful" (Ya-Sin 36:58). Beneath this peace from the Merciful Lord, all kinds of blessings are enfolded.
